extra.message: POST /api/sqlivuln passes the JSON username directly into an SQL statement using an f-string. An attacker can terminate the quoted value and inject SQL predicates or UNION queries to retrieve database contents.

POST /api/sstivuln concatenates the attacker-controlled mathexp value into Jinja2 template source and calls render(). This unsandboxed template evaluation permits arbitrary expressions and access to Python objects, enabling server-side code execution.

cwe: CWE-1336: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements Used in a Template Engine

extra.message: POST /api/lfivuln forwards the JSON filename through fetchfile() directly to open(name). No directory restriction or path validation exists. Absolute paths and traversal sequences allow unauthenticated callers to read arbitrary text files accessible to the server; their contents are returned in the response.

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

extra.message: POST /api/rfivuln passes the attacker-controlled imagelink to requests.get() without restricting destinations. An unauthenticated caller can request loopback, private-network, or cloud metadata HTTP endpoints through the server and receive their response bodies.

The outbound request explicitly sets verify=False, disabling TLS certificate validation. A network attacker can impersonate an HTTPS destination and intercept or alter fetched content. See [Requests TLS documentation](https://requests.readthedocs.io/en/stable/user/advanced/#ssl-cert-verification).

An unauthenticated caller can supply an imagelink whose server sends an arbitrarily large or continuously growing response. The response is buffered without a size limit, allowing memory exhaustion and worker occupation. timeout=2 does not impose a total download deadline; a server can keep sending data before each read timeout. See [Requests timeout documentation](https://requests.readthedocs.io/en/latest/user/quickstart/#timeouts).

cwe: CWE-770: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling

extra.message: The attacker-controlled filename is read to EOF without a size limit or regular-file check. On Unix systems, submitting /dev/zero causes an indefinitely growing read that can exhaust server memory. Large readable files can also exhaust memory before a response is produced.

cwe: CWE-789: Memory Allocation with Excessive Size Value

extra.message: The response includes complete USERS rows obtained with SELECT *, including the PASSWORD column defined in custom_db.py. The supplied password is checked only for nonemptiness and never verified. If user records exist, anyone knowing a username can retrieve that user's stored password value without SQL injection. The bundled initialization contains invalid INSERT statements, so this disclosure depends on records being present.

SQLite exception text is returned directly to unauthenticated callers. Malformed username values can trigger SQL errors that reveal database identifiers and query diagnostics, helping an attacker construct SQL injection payloads.

cwe: CWE-209: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information

extra.message: POST /api/hhivuln prints the complete request.headers collection to stdout without redaction. Requests containing Authorization, Cookie, or API-key headers therefore expose those credentials to application logs and their readers.

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File

extra.message: The documented startup path enables debug=True while binding to all network interfaces. Reachable clients can trigger unhandled errors, such as invalid Jinja2 template syntax, and receive debug tracebacks exposing source and internal details. The development debugger also introduces an interactive execution surface subject to its access controls.
